name: Piktochart
tagline: Assemble infographics and reports from data, text, and reusable visual blocks

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 1 owner plus 3 members; 2 PNG downloads; 60 AI credits; 1 GB storage; 1 folder; unlimited projects.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 500 AI credits/member, unlimited PNG downloads and 100 GB storage/member.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: 1,000 AI credits/member, unlimited PNG/PDF/PPT downloads and 250 GB storage/member.

tiers.name: Education
tiers.notes: Published as $39.99 per member per year.

tiers.name: Campus
tiers.limits: Custom campus deployment with a 3,000-seat minimum.

tiers.name: Nonprofit
tiers.notes: Published as $60 per member per year.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 1 owner + 3 members, 2 PNG downloads, 60 AI credits, 1 GB storage, 1 folder and unlimited projects.
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual for commercial plans; Education and Nonprofit are annual; Campus/Enterprise are custom
pricing.hiddenCosts: Commercial tiers charge per member after the free workspace allowance. Campus has a 3,000-seat minimum, and purchases are generally non-refundable.

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Piktochart, assemble infographics and reports from data, text, and reusable visual blocks. The hard boundary is templates, charts, asset library, brand controls, and hosted publishing, plus editor polish, assets, collaboration, and distribution.
coreLoopDIY: Assemble infographics and reports from data, text, and reusable visual blocks on a canvas, edit text and media, and export a finished SVG or PDF.
whatYouLose: templates, charts, asset library, brand controls, and hosted publishing
moatNotes: editor polish, assets, collaboration, and distribution
ongoingBurden: canvas correctness, fonts, exports, templates, asset rights, multiplayer state, and accessibility
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Piktochart because people pay for a vast ready-made design system and a collaboration surface that behaves predictably under deadline. The recurring cost buys canvas correctness, fonts, exports, templates, asset rights, multiplayer state, and accessibility, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Penpot
priorArt.desc: Mature open-source collaborative design platform with SVG-native editing.

alternatives.name: Adobe Express Free
alternatives.desc: Good for visual reports and infographic-style pages, with fewer data widgets but a clean free export path.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the Adobe Express desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Adobe Firefly models power the generative features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, libraries and brand assets live in Adobe's cloud; exports include image, PDF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Adobe Express has fewer data widgets, chart controls and report-specific blocks than Piktochart.

alternatives.name: Canva Free
alternatives.desc: The strongest free substitute for block-built infographics and reports, with charts, templates, PDF export, and collaborative editing.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install Canva's desktop/mobile app.
facts.engines: Canva AI and Magic Studio provide generative tools; Canva does not publish a complete provider/model map for the free editor.
facts.dataFormat: Designs, uploads, folders and brand assets live in Canva's cloud; users export common image, PDF, presentation and video formats.
facts.gapVsPaid: Canva is less purpose-built for data-driven reports and infographics, especially when charts must stay coherent across many pages.

alternatives.name: Desygner Free
alternatives.desc: Templates, charts, multipage PDFs, and reusable brand assets for a small team; the editor is less refined.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.engines: Desygner's terms identify OpenAI-backed AI features.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads, fonts and brand assets live in Desygner's cloud; designs export as image or PDF files.
facts.gapVsPaid: Desygner's charts and data-storytelling controls are less refined than Piktochart's infographic workflow.

alternatives.name: VistaCreate Starter
alternatives.desc: Fine for visual one-pagers and simple infographics; weaker when the document needs real data storytelling.

facts.install: Hosted signup in a browser, or install the mobile app.
facts.dataFormat: Projects, uploads and the single Brand Kit live in VistaCreate's cloud; exports include image, GIF and video files.
facts.gapVsPaid: VistaCreate is weak for data-rich reports, live charts and structured infographic storytelling.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Penpot
rejectedAlternatives.desc: It can draw an infographic manually, just as a lathe can make a spoon; it lacks the reusable data-and-report workflow.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal design canvas DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Piktochart in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, React, Tailwind CSS, IndexedDB, and SVG; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: assemble infographics and reports from data, text, and reusable visual blocks on a canvas, edit text and media, and export a finished SVG or PDF.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a fixed-size SVG canvas with zoom, pan, selection, alignment, and snapping.
Support text, rectangles, circles, images, groups, layers, and reusable components.
Add a small set of high-quality starter layouts relevant to the product category.
Implement undo, redo, autosave, and import or export of a portable project JSON file.
Export SVG and print-ready PDF without rasterizing text unnecessarily.
Keep all assets local and display missing-font warnings before export.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer editing.
Deliberately leave out a commercial stock-asset library.
Deliberately leave out enterprise brand controls and approval workflows.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
